The '''2026 The Hundred season''' was the sixth season of [[The Hundred (cricket)|The Hundred]], a professional franchise [[100-ball cricket]] tournament involving eight men's and women's teams located in major cities across the United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/cricket/news/12123/13493919/the-hundred-mens-and-womens-squads-for-2026-season-which-runs-from-july-21-august-16-live-on-sky-sports |title=The Hundred: Men's and women's squads for 2026 season which runs from July 21-August 16 live on Sky Sports |work=[[Sky Sports]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/c3r4rdq8523o |title=What will The Hundred look like in 2026? |work=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref>

The previous year's women's tournament was won for the first time by the [[Northern Superchargers]], while the men's [[Oval Invincibles]] won their third consecutive title.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cvg02n9lll5o |title=Invincibles win third Hundred men's title in a row |work=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricinfo.com/series/the-hundred-women-s-competition-2025-1471001/northern-superchargers-women-vs-southern-brave-women-final-1471069/match-report |title=Cross, Sutherland level up as Northern Superchargers clinch Women's Hundred title |work=[[Cricinfo]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref>

[[Trent Rockets|Trent Rockets women]] and [[Manchester Super Giants|Manchester Super Giants men]] won their respective titles for the first time.<ref>{{cite web |last=Miller |first=Andrew |date=16 August 2026 |title=Adams excels as Rockets surge to maiden Women's Hundred title |url=https://www.cricinfo.com/series/the-hundred-women-s-competition-2026-1521193/sunrisers-leeds-women-vs-trent-rockets-women-final-1521230/match-report |work=[[Cricinfo]] |access-date=17 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Wynne |first=Ffion |date=16 August 2026 |title=Rockets crush Sunrisers for first women's Hundred title |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cdj00mw7l20o |work=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=17 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Trent Rockets thrash SunRisers Leeds at Lord's to win women's title for first time |url=https://www.skysports.com/the-hundred/news/36888/13573734/the-hundred-trent-rockets-thrash-sunrisers-leeds-at-lords-to-win-womens-title-for-first-time |work=[[Sky Sports]] |date=16 August 2026 ==Background==
===Finance===
In late 2025, the ECB finalised deals that valued the eight teams at over £975 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ecb.co.uk/news/4413484/the-hundred-team-partnerships-completed |title=The Hundred team partnerships completed |work=[[England and Wales Cricket Board]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref> This restructuring was designed to secure the long-term financial health of the game, with over £500 million set to be reinvested into English and Welsh cricket, including a £50 million commitment to grassroots initiatives.

The 2026 season is the first where '''TeamCos'''—consisting of the investors and host venues—assumes full operational control. The buyers include a mix of [[Indian Premier League]] (IPL) owners, American private equity firms, and tech entrepreneurs. The completed partnerships for the 2026 season are as follows:<ref>{{cite web |first=Roller |last=Matt |date=13 February 2025 |url=https://www.cricinfo.com/story/hundred-equity-sale-explainer-who-has-bought-what-how-much-1473079 |title=Hundred sale explainer: Who has bought what and for how much? |work=[[Cricinfo]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref>
* London Spirit: A consortium of Silicon Valley tech entrepreneurs (including executives from Google and Microsoft) bought the 49% stake for £145m (the highest valuation).
* Oval Invincibles: Reliance Industries (owners of Mumbai Indians) bought the 49% stake for £60m.
* Manchester Originals: RPSG Group (owners of Lucknow Super Giants) took a 70% stake for £81m, with Lancashire retaining 30%.
* Northern Superchargers: Sun TV Network (owners of Sunrisers Hyderabad) purchased 100% of the team for £100m.
* Birmingham Phoenix: Knighthead Capital (owners of Birmingham City FC) acquired 49% for £40m.
* Welsh Fire: Sanjay Govil (owner of Washington Freedom) bought 50% for £40m.
* Southern Brave: GMR Group (co-owners of Delhi Capitals) bought 49% and is also taking over the host county, Hampshire.
* Trent Rockets: [[Cain (company)|Cain]] & Ares Management jointly bought 49% for just under £40m.

=== Competition format ===
As in previous editions, eight city-based teams will compete for the men's and women's titles during 21 July to 16 August 2026.

The teams will play a total of 64 matches in the group stage (32 men's, 32 women's). All matches will be held on the same day at the same grounds, with one ticket granting access to both men's and women's contests.

Each team will play four matches at home and four away, including one match against every other side in the competition and a bonus match against their nearest regional rivals. After the league stage, the top three teams will progress to the knockout stage to decide the champions. The second- and third-placed teams will face each other in the eliminator at The Oval in London. The winner of the eliminator then met the league-topping team in the final at Lord's.

===Player selection process===
For the 2026 season of The Hundred, player recruitment is conducted through a structured, three-stage system designed to balance competitive fairness with strategic flexibility for teams.<ref name="PP">{{cite web |url=https://www.thehundred.com/info/how-player-selection-works |title=The Hundred Player Slection-Explained |work=The Hundred |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref>

====Pre-auction signings and retention====
Each franchise may make up to four pre-auction signings or retentions between mid-November and the end of January. Of these, a maximum of three can be direct signings limited to overseas players or England centrally contracted players, while at least one must be a retention from the existing squad, which can include domestic players as well. Teams may include up to two England centrally contracted players and up to two overseas players among their pre-auction signings. No "right to match (RTM)" option is available at this stage.<ref name="PP"/>

To maintain balance and competitiveness, pre-auction signings reduce each team's available salary cap ahead of the auction according to a tiered cumulative deduction model. For the men's competition, deductions range from £350,000 for one signing to £950,000 for four signings. In the women's competition, corresponding deductions range from £130,000 to £360,000.<ref name="PP"/>

====Auction====
Following the direct signing window, an auction will be held on 11 & 12 March to complete squad formation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=First Hundred auction to span two days in March |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/cricket/articles/cedweq6zj52o}}</ref> Teams are required to recruit the remaining players within their salary cap: 16–18 players for men's squads and 15 for women's squads. For the 2026 season, the overall salary pot is set at £2.05 million for men's teams and £880,000 for women's teams, reflecting increased investment in player payments.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricinfo.com/story/the-hundred-to-introduce-player-auction-for-2026-season-1509479 |title=The Hundred to introduce player auction for 2026 season |work=[[Cricinfo]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cricbuzz.com/cricket-news/136149/the-hundred-set-for-first-player-auction-in-march-2026-cricbuzzcom |title=The Hundred set for first player auction in March 2026 |work=[[Cricbuzz]] |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref>

====Vitality Wildcard====
After the main auction, the Vitality Wildcard offers teams an additional mechanism to recruit players based on strong performances in the domestic [[T20 Blast]] competitions. Players who are not selected in the main auction can still earn contracts through this pathway, reinforcing the link between domestic form and participation in The Hundred.<ref name="PP"/>

==== Replacements ====
* '''Birmingham Phoenix:'''
** [[Matt Montgomery (cricketer)|Matt Montgomery]] replaced [[Ethan Brookes]] due to injury.
** [[Joe Weatherley]] replaced [[Jacob Bethell]] due to injury.
** [[Ben Dwarshuis]] replaced [[Mustafizur Rahman]] due to injury.

* '''London Spirit:'''
** [[Andrew Tye]] replaced [[Adam Hose]] due to injury.
** [[Joe Moores]] replaced [[Tymal Mills]] due to injury.

* '''Manchester Super Giants:'''
** [[Michael Bracewell (cricketer)|Michael Bracewell]] replaced [[Aiden Markram]] due to personal reasons.

* '''MI London:'''
** [[Josh Philippe]] replaced [[Sherfane Rutherford]] for one match due to prior commitments.
** [[Sikandar Raza]] replaced [[Rashid Khan]] for three matches due to international commitments.

* '''Southern Brave:'''
** [[Moeen Ali]] replaced [[Thomas Rew (cricketer)|Thomas Rew]] due to injury.

* '''Sunrisers Leeds:'''
** [[Graham Clark (English cricketer)|Graham Clark]] replaced [[Tom Alsop]] due to injury.
** [[James Fuller (cricketer, born 1990)|James Fuller]] replaced [[Reece Topley]] due to injury.

* '''Trent Rockets:'''
** [[Mohammad Amir]] replaced [[David Payne (cricketer)|David Payne]] due to injury.
** [[Calvin Harrison (cricketer)|Calvin Harrison]] replaced [[Brad Currie]] due to injury.
** [[Matt Milnes]] replaced [[Tom Banton]] due to injury.
